item.title: Here's what Siri AI looks like on HomePod, per leak (2 minute read)
item.description: Code discovered in HomePod 27 suggests Apple is actively preparing Siri AI for HomePod, including redesigned animated status lights that reflect the assistant's new visual identity. Although the feature isn't currently enabled, the software contains the necessary framework, adding weight to rumors that new HomePod and Apple TV hardware launching later this year will support Siri AI. Apple's silence about bringing the feature to existing HomePods suggests the upgraded assistant will likely require new hardware.

item.title: Six New Google Flow Tools Built by Industry Creatives (4 minute read)
item.description: Google has released six new Google Flow Tools built with creative leaders from architecture, sound design, and digital content to support their specific workflows. The tools include Mondo Sónico for synchronized ambiance and foley, CaptionCast and ThumbnailForge for automated captions and social thumbnails, Surface for real-time architectural texture mapping, and CollageMotion Pro and SwissFlow Studio for animated collages and Swiss-style motion graphics. Users can try, duplicate, or build their own custom tools by describing the workflow they need.

item.title: Adobe just made Claude far more useful for PDFs by bringing Acrobat tools directly into the chat (3 minute read)
item.description: Adobe has expanded its Claude plugin by integrating Acrobat tools, allowing users to edit, organize, convert, redact, and review PDFs directly within Claude, alongside an interactive PDF editor and AI-powered document review. The company also added Photoshop, Lightroom, Express, and Firefly tools to Google Gemini, enabling users to edit images and designs without leaving the chat interface.

item.title: Putting the User Back into AI Evaluation (10 minute read)
item.description: Three researchers on Microsoft's AI team argue that while machine evaluations confirm a response meets set criteria, only users can judge whether it actually worked for them. Qualitative conversations with real users exposed gaps between what builders assumed was good and what users valued, including tone, context, and a fear of generic output. The team built a shared loss-pattern taxonomy and multi-turn evaluations that treat entire conversations, rather than single responses, as the unit of measurement.

item.title: Design Engineering with Maggie Appleton (8 minute read)
item.description: AI is changing how designers work, but not what makes great design: human judgment, problem-solving, and clear thinking remain essential. Start with familiar patterns, sketch ideas by hand, build interactive AI-powered prototypes, and treat AI as a collaborator that accelerates exploration while requiring constant oversight.

item.description: Understand the minds you're designing for and the mind you're designing with.

item.title: First McDonald's, Now Disney is Dejoying Its Store Designs (3 minute read)
item.description: Disney Wonders, the redesigned flagship gift shop at Disneyland Paris, replaced its vibrant, chaotic look with clean brand-themed zones for Disney, Pixar, Marvel, and Star Wars. Despite a multi-stage launch with influencer and cast-member previews, public reaction has called the store as drab and clinical as an airport shop. The redesign is framed as part of a broader "dejoying" trend seen at McDonald's, Burger King, and Starbucks, where playful branding has given way to minimalist interiors.

item.title: What a UX Designer Learned from Building Apps with AI (5 minute read)
item.description: A UX designer at Singapore's GovTech spent months building small working apps solo using the AI app builder Lovable. Building a real-time planning-poker tool exposed AI's limits: the assistant kept failing until a developer explained he needed a WebSocket, the technical term that finally unblocked progress. The experiment's lesson was that AI accelerates prototyping but doesn't replace design judgment or engineering expertise, especially for public-sector systems that must run reliably at scale.

item.title: Wu Xinlin's editorial illustrations show solitude in a whole new light (3 minute read)
item.description: Chinese illustrator Wu Xinlin explores the complexity of solitude through surreal, symbolic illustrations that blend humor, unease, and emotional growth, creating deeply human editorial work that celebrates introspection without romanticizing it.

item.title: Design Effectiveness in 2026 (1 minute read)
item.description: Clearleft is repeating a 2019 survey of over 400 designers to find out how the pandemic and AI have reshaped what makes design effective.

item.title: People are treating Apple's macOS 27 wallpaper 'design fail' like a true crime mystery to be solved (2 minute read)
item.description: Some macOS 27 Golden Gate users believe the default live wallpaper contains a visual glitch where a background building appears to overlap a foreground rock, though it's unclear whether it's an editing mistake or a natural perspective effect.

item.title: Meta introduces camera-free AI glasses (3 minute read)
item.description: Meta introduced Ray-Ban Meta Audio, camera-free AI glasses that support music, calls, speech translation, and its Muse assistant, offering an alternative to smart glasses that can record people without their consent. Removing the cameras makes the frames slimmer and lighter at 43 grams, with adjustable temple tips, swappable nose pads, and a battery life of up to 12 hours. Starting at $349, the glasses come in Clubmaster and Burbank styles with prescription options.

item.title: macOS 27 gives you more control over Liquid Glass (3 minute read)
item.description: macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a customizable Liquid Glass appearance slider that lets users adjust the system's transparency from highly clear to more opaque, changing the look of the Dock, widgets, sidebars, toolbars, and apps like Music and Podcasts with a single system-wide setting. The update gives users more control over the Mac's visual style while preserving the modern Liquid Glass design language.

item.title: Adobe Premiere, One of the iPhone's Best Video-Editing Apps, is Now on Android (3 minute read)
item.description: Adobe is bringing its redesigned Premiere video-editing app to Android, nearly a year after its iPhone debut, replacing Premiere Rush, which loses support September 30. Layouts adapt across devices, pairing footage and a multitrack timeline side by side on foldables while still running on candy-bar phones like the Pixel. The app is free with no login required, though Firefly-powered features like Generative Fill require paid generative credits once the monthly allotment runs out.

item.title: UX-Context Design: Using UX Knowledge to Inform AI-Generated Design (8 minute read)
item.description: As more interface work turns AI-generated, research and design output shifts from human-facing deliverables toward curated context that guides AI, dubbed UX-context design. DESIGN.md, which Google Labs open-sourced in April 2026 from its Stitch tool, encodes a product's visual identity for AI tools in exact values and plain-language guidance. A hypothetical broader file, UX.md, would add research findings, interaction standards, a glossary, and user and world models as a continuously updated source.

item.title: Modernizing a legacy system? Your before/after isn't the case study (5 minute read)
item.description: Strong modernization case studies focus less on before-and-after visuals and more on the design decisions behind them, highlighting the judgment calls that shaped the final product rather than the process or visual refresh alone. Employers want to understand what changed because of the designer's thinking, not just that an outdated interface now looks modern.

item.title: Nothing has changed other than how we talk about it (8 minute read)
item.description: Agentic AI can dramatically speed up the research and problem-definition phases of Design Thinking by analyzing assumptions, synthesizing evidence, and pressure-testing ideas, but human judgment remains essential for validating outputs and making design decisions. Rather than replacing designers, AI shifts their role from generating information to evaluating evidence, challenging assumptions, and deciding what should be built.

item.description: A system that preserves the act of drawing itself, where every gesture is remembered, and every image continues to evolve.

item.description: The visual dictionary of AI art keywords — one word, one image, and free to browse. Master prompt keywords for Midjourney, Google Nano Banana, GPT Image, FLUX, and Stable Diffusion.

item.title: Named Colors with Documented Histories (Website)
item.description: One color a day, told as it ought to be told: with its provenance, its chemistry, and the people who paid for it in poison.

item.title: Design Systems are a Collection of Decisions (10 minute read)
item.description: Design systems amount to collections of already-made decisions, so mechanical checks can prove straight from the artifact whether an AI agent used real components and correct tokens. Judgment-based evals still have an answer key when the system has documented a decision, like a required confirmation pattern for destructive actions. Visual evals work against a known reference, but deciding whether a new visual direction deserves to exist should stay with people.

item.title: Spatial UI Design: Tips and Best Practices (21 minute read)
item.description: Augmented reality design differs from screen-based UX, demanding attention to physical space, bodily comfort, and the cognitive load added to real-world distractions. UX consultant Frank Spillers' guidelines favor real-world physics, direct hand gestures over menus, context-aware triggers, and short, interruptible interactions. Content should stay within about 30 degrees of a user's central field of view, never past 50, and sit between 1.25 and 5 meters away.

item.title: Industrial Designer Alberto Essesi's Pen for Precision Sketching (1 minute read)
item.description: Alberto Essesi's satin-finished aluminum Exclamation Pen and matching rest feature a severely tapered point that keeps the tip visible for precision sketching.

item.title: This Secret Brooklyn Archive Contains a Trove of Design Rarities. Here Are 10 Exceptional Finds (8 minute read)
item.description: Collectible design gallery R & Company has opened Building 86, its 16,000-square-foot storage warehouse in the Brooklyn Navy Yard, to the public by appointment for the first time.

item.title: McLaren's new logo looks like a luxury fashion brand (3 minute read)
item.description: McLaren has unveiled a refined brand identity that modernizes its wordmark while drawing inspiration from the signage of the McLaren family's original service station, balancing heritage with a more contemporary look. The redesign also retains the iconic Speedmark for its racing and golf divisions, reinforcing brand continuity while signaling a new chapter for the company.

item.title: Bringing Emoji into the Next Era of Expression (5 minute read)
item.description: Noto 3D redraws emoji by hand rather than automating the jump into three dimensions, keeping expression readable at 18 pixels instead of chasing photorealism. Rotating the camera exposed legacy mistakes, including a poodle with three legs, and research showed that anatomical detail slows how fast people read emotion. An AI contrast audit flagged where darker skin tones vanish in dark mode across all 3,977 characters, and the library ships open source.

item.title: The bold new Apple Music logo signals the end of minimalism (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple has quietly introduced a bold new Apple Music wordmark alongside the launch of Apple Music Hall in London, replacing its minimalist branding with a retro-inspired, lowercase logo that signals a shift toward a more expressive visual identity. The redesign reflects Apple's growing embrace of bolder, more playful aesthetics and could hint at the direction of its future design language.

item.title: Props Are Not a Design System (5 minute read)
item.description: Inline styling — via Tailwind classes or style attributes — makes every component a one-off decision, breaking visual consistency, semantics, and maintainability. The proposed fix is defining styles once through named "variants" (complete, self-contained visual definitions) and "modifiers" (controlled variations like size), rather than overriding styles at the call site. Following this discipline across any UI kit naturally produces a real design system, turning scattered styling decisions into a reusable, consistent structure.

item.title: Please don't stretch your app for foldables (9 minute read)
item.description: Foldable devices require apps to adapt to changing screen sizes, orientations, and postures with responsive layouts, multi-pane interfaces, and hinge-aware designs that preserve context and usability instead of simply stretching existing mobile UIs. By designing around available space rather than specific devices, teams can create experiences that work consistently across phones, foldables, tablets, and desktop-sized windows while following platform-specific layout conventions.

item.title: Decision Paralysis, Lost Conviction and No Juniors: What Brand Creative Leaders Say AI is Exposing (7 minute read)
item.description: Brand Perspectives 2026, a MikeTeevee report drawing on in-house leaders at Wayfair, DoorDash, Intuit, O2, Canva, and Rivian, found that AI accelerated problems that predate it. Teams generating endless variations at near-zero cost now stall on choosing, while trimmed junior roles take the mid-level pipeline with them. Efficiency has not lightened the load: everyone reports working twice as hard, with handoffs still run off spreadsheets.

item.description: Create precise, harmonious typography with Precise Type. Explore type scales, font sizes, line heights, and letter spacing – then export the CSS.

item.description: Free browser-based image effects editor with 75+ effects. Turn photos into dither, halftone, ASCII art, pixel art, and voxel graphics.

item.title: Originality is overrated. Elaboration is the thing (5 minute read)
item.description: Research suggests that creative work delivers the strongest business results not through originality alone, but through elaboration—the careful refinement and execution that turn a good idea into a polished, effective campaign. As AI makes generating novel ideas easier, human value increasingly lies in the thousands of design decisions, craftsmanship, and attention to detail that set exceptional work apart from merely original work.

item.title: On making room for craft (5 minute read)
item.description: Reducing scope instead of quality means treating a complete, reliable user experience as non-negotiable while cutting optional features when time is limited. Teams should estimate and prioritize the full interaction—including loading states, errors, and edge cases—assign ownership for polishing core flows, and make deliberate trade-offs so products don't rely on last-minute fixes to feel complete.

item.title: Eight Lessons for Brand Builders in the Age of AI (9 minute read)
item.description: Forty-four hours of Brand Builders Summit 2026, across 48 speakers, circle one question: what makes a brand builder irreplaceable?

item.title: Jenna Arts on why the stumbling, silly, ordinary human is the only one worth drawing (7 minute read)
item.description: Illustrator Jenna Arts celebrates imperfection and everyday humanity, arguing that the authenticity, personality, and flaws of human-made art are what make it meaningful in an AI-driven world.

item.title: Apple leak claims 20th-anniversary iPhone will ape a design formula from a decade ago (3 minute read)
item.description: Apple is reportedly testing a major display redesign for its rumored 20th-anniversary iPhone Pro models, featuring larger quad-curved, nearly borderless screens with a smaller display cutout. While the current iPhone 18 Pro focuses on internal upgrades, the 2027 models could deliver a more dramatic visual refresh—though the leak reflects early prototypes, and the design may still change.

item.title: Projects Redesigned: From Folder to Conversation (5 minute read)
item.description: Claude Code projects shift from folders to a coordinator that scopes a request, delegates it across parallel threads, reviews the outputs, and assembles the result. Each thread runs as a cloud session on its own branch, and a shared memory carries context between them. The beta opens to select Claude Pro and Max subscribers, expanding to more plans later.

item.title: Adobe Patents a System That Writes AI Prompts from Whatever Your Cursor Hovers Over (3 minute read)
item.description: Adobe's patent application describes a system that reads the context around whatever a cursor hovers over and writes the AI prompt automatically, before any click happens. The system generates content preemptively, so results appear instantly when the user finally clicks. The trade-off is wasted work every time the system guesses wrong.

item.title: Designing with AI (6 minute read)
item.description: AI expanded what designers can make, but used carelessly, it only produces average work faster. Help Scout's answer was a design.md capturing 15 years of judgment, plus a design system rebuilt over two weeks to make 200-plus primitives legible to LLMs. Within three months, designers were coding components, running local environments, and shipping selected improvements to production themselves.

item.title: The Design GM (8 minute read)
item.description: Designers can prepare for General Manager (GM) roles by expanding their focus beyond design to take ownership of business outcomes, operations, and talent. Adopting a GM mindset means being accountable for customer value, cross-functional decisions, budgets, and long-term results, allowing designers to evolve from executing work to shaping business strategy and driving organizational success.

item.description: A curated library of production-ready components, creative coding tutorials, design process frameworks, AI workflow guides, and a live theme generator.

item.title: The mascots, design and visual history of Wikipedia, the encyclopedia that puts functionality above aesthetics (15 minute read)
item.description: Wikipedia's enduring design is built around simplicity, accessibility, and trust, evolving only subtly while remaining highly customizable and supported by a passionate global community of volunteers. Beyond the encyclopedia itself, its visual identity extends through iconic branding like the puzzle globe, community-created mascots, creative projects, and campaigns that celebrate Wikipedia as a collaborative, human-powered ecosystem rather than just a website.

item.title: NEW STANDARD.S gives climate journalism critic Brandmelder an identity (3 minute read)
item.description: Brandmelder's new identity was designed to position the climate journalism watchdog as a credible, neutral media critic rather than an activist organization. Built around a customizable dot-grid system, restrained typography, and a subtle color palette inspired by climate stripes, the branding emphasizes consistency, objectivity, and ease of use while helping the project reach mainstream news audiences.

item.title: AI Can Build Your UI. Now Figma Can Tell It When It Screwed Up (4 minute read)
item.description: Applitools' integration lets a Figma frame URL serve as the visual baseline, matching the test viewport and flagging where an implementation drifts from the approved design. The same September 15 release expands its Eyes MCP Server so coding agents can inspect, review, and resolve visual tests from chat. Code that runs is not the same as code that matches the design, and Figma becomes the reference that settles it.

item.title: Your Presentations Feel Lifeless Because They're Missing a Villain (6 minute read)
item.description: The villain in a design story is never a person: it is the status quo, and it is already winning when the story opens.

item.title: Here's why Apple scrapped its shorter Apple Pencil designed for iPhone Duo: report (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple scrapped its planned iPhone Duo-specific Apple Pencil due to technical issues.

item.title: Disney's first CTO led an AI startup it once accused of copying its characters (1 minute read)
item.description: Disney has appointed former Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand as its first chief technology officer, reporting to CEO Josh D'Amaro. The hire comes after Disney accused Character.AI of using its copyrighted characters without permission and demanded their removal. Anand previously held leadership roles at Meta and spent 15 years at Microsoft, bringing consumer technology and AI experience to Disney's push to make technology a larger part of its entertainment business.

item.title: Google's new ‘CC' is an AI agent that helps families run their households (3 minute read)
item.description: Google is testing a family-focused version of CC that turns shared emails and messages into daily briefings, calendar events, and tasks for up to six household members. The agent has its own Google account and can help fill out permission slips, create shopping lists, and plan meals, while each person controls what information they share. The experiment is available through a waitlist for US adults with personal Google accounts.

item.title: Anthropic Tries to Make Claude Stickier with Launch of Docs and Slides (5 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Docs and Slides, a rich-text editor letting users draft documents and presentations from chat while Claude asks clarifying questions and comments on its choices. Files land in the Artifacts tab, export to Word, PDF, Google Docs, or Markdown, and support real-time collaboration, though Team and Enterprise still lack version history. Analysts see it as an attempt to make Claude stickier by pulling productivity work into the AI, unlike Microsoft and Google embedding AI into existing office tools.

item.title: Lost dog—or lost designer? (8 minute read)
item.description: AI-generated design is not inherently ethical or unethical—the morality depends on the context, including whether automation was necessary, who benefits, who is harmed, and whether it replaces existing design work or simply enables people without the resources to access design. The more meaningful ethical question is when its use becomes unjust and how the costs and benefits of automation are distributed across designers, businesses, customers, and society.

item.title: A Simple Guide to Calm UI (2 minute read)
item.description: Calm UI comes down to two core rules: avoid cascading loading states and skip toasts in favor of showing an action's effect directly in the list. Four bonus rules round it out: no error toasts, pinning modals that change height to the top, letting Enter submit forms, and auto-focusing a dialog's first input.

item.title: Foundations maxxing: Why your design system is not ready for AI (7 minute read)
item.description: AI can dramatically speed up product development, but only if it's built on a solid design system. Teams should prioritize auditing and strengthening foundations—such as design tokens, components, documentation, decision logs, and design-to-code pipelines—before making systems machine-readable, while emphasizing collaboration with developers and a UX-first mindset to avoid creating inconsistent, unscalable products.

item.title: AI Render Studio for Architects (Website)
item.description: Rendervi is built for architecture and visualization teams that care about quality, speed, and control. Enhance architectural renders, change materials, or push a model preview toward photorealism without losing the design intent.

item.title: Screen Recorder for Mac (Website)
item.description: A Mac screen recorder for clear, polished videos without complicated editing. Camera, mic, system audio, captions, 4K export, and shareable links.

item.title: One More Thing About the iPhone 18 Pro: The Bigger/Smaller Dynamic Island (2 minute read)
item.description: The iPhone 18 Pro moves its Face ID infrared camera beneath the display, allowing Apple to shrink the Dynamic Island cutout while expanding its usable space to support up to three simultaneous Live Activities. Although the pixels above the hidden sensor appear slightly softer than the rest of the display, the change marks another step toward Apple's long-term goal of a true edge-to-edge, all-screen iPhone.

item.title: Better Icon and Label Alignment (3 minute read)
item.description: When list item text wraps to multiple lines, a centered icon ends up looking misaligned against the first line of text. Switching align-items to start and offsetting the icon with a translateY calculated from the lh unit keeps it aligned regardless of icon or font size. The same lh-based offset, paired with aspect-ratio, flex-shrink, and background-size: contain, fixes alignment for icons built as pseudo-elements too.

item.title: The Paradox of Clarity: Why Data Design is Our Most Treacherous Medium (5 minute read)
item.description: Data visualization is having a cultural moment, with MoMA's Full Disclosure, Refik Anadol's Dataland, and OMA/AMO's Diagrams each treating data as translation, aesthetic medium, and political instrument. Across all three, the real danger isn't scarce information, but the false authority clarity lends to flawed data, as Lombroso's debunked 19th-century iris charts once showed. The next phase of data design may favor curation over abundance and structural transparency over deceptive clarity, trading spectacle for restraint.

item.title: This Artist Turns Grief, Memory, and Isolation into Surreal Images That Feel Like Pages Torn from an Unfinished Dream (1 minute read)
item.description: Journal of Emptiness turns grief, memory, and isolation into surreal, wordless images paired with short poetic captions that read like fragments of an unfinished, dreamlike novel.

item.title: Download the iPhone Duo's official light and dark wallpapers here (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple has made the official iPhone Duo wallpapers available through the Xcode 27.1 beta simulator, allowing anyone to download all four light and dark versions without owning the device.

item.title: Light & Magic: The Birth of Art Photography (6 minute read)
item.description: Tate Modern's Light & Magic gathers over 200 vintage prints by more than 80 artists, reframing Pictorialism as its own movement rather than a bridge to Modernism.

item.title: Pinterest Restyle Reimagines Your Room (2 minute read)
item.description: Pinterest has unveiled Restyle, an AI-powered feature that lets users upload a photo of their room and explore how different design ideas would look in their own space. Users can test furniture, decor, paint colors, and lighting, remove or swap individual objects, or try a completely different style. Launching in beta in the US and Canada, Restyle brings Pinterest Intelligence directly into the consumer experience, helping people compare options and turn inspiration into more concrete plans for their homes.

item.title: Publish Weave Tools to the Figma Community (1 minute read)
item.description: Figma now lets users build custom Weave tools—generative AI workflows created in Figma Weave—and publish them to the Figma Community for others to use directly on the canvas in Figma Design. These tools support repeatable image and vector generation at scale, and people can browse the Community to see tools others have built. While any output type, including video and 3D renderings, can be published to the Community, only image and vector generation tools work within Figma Design itself.

item.title: Samsung starts rolling out Android 17 with One UI 9, confirms initial list of Galaxy devices (2 minute read)
item.description: Samsung has officially begun rolling out One UI 9, based on Android 17, starting with the Galaxy S26 series after a four-month beta. The update introduces new Galaxy AI features, including My FanCam, Creative Studio, Now Brief enhancements, improved privacy and security tools, and easier access to warranty information. Samsung says the update will gradually expand to more Galaxy phones and tablets, including recent S-series, Fold, Flip, and Tab models.

item.title: The Invisible Side of Design Engineering (2 minute read)
item.description: Design engineering has no fixed definition, and social media makes it look like little more than building animated eye-candy components. Day-to-day work leans heavily on invisible priorities like accessibility, responsiveness, performance, and the edge cases only real users surface. A great experience often comes down to unglamorous effort, like spending an afternoon on an accessibility fix or making a landing page load slightly faster.

item.title: Five eras of UX design and the lessons to keep in the AI era (15 minute read)
item.description: User experience design has evolved through five major eras—from Human Factors and the Web to Mobile, Design Systems, and AI—each contributing a lasting lesson while leaving behind habits that later became limitations. Designers should focus less on producing interfaces and more on shaping systems, information architecture, constraints, and the rules that govern intelligent experiences, as these are becoming the most valuable skills in the AI era. Rather than replacing UX, AI continues the historical pattern of making creation cheaper while shifting designers' value toward higher-level thinking and decision-making.

item.title: Seven lines of client feedback that knock you sideways, and how to stop them living rent-free in your head (6 minute read)
item.description: Clients often give confusing or unhelpful feedback because of uncertainty, internal politics, or a lack of design knowledge rather than problems with the work itself. Common situations include vague requests like “make it look less designed,” Canva comparisons, hidden budgets, feedback by committee, and indecisive comments such as “I'll know it when I see it.” Responding with calm questions, clarifying underlying concerns, setting expectations early, and guiding clients through the design process can turn frustrating feedback into more productive conversations.

item.description: An interactive 3D keyboard for learning the keyboard shortcuts of the apps you use every day. Pick a tool, hover a shortcut, and watch the keys light up.

item.title: Planning with Agents: Divided Worlds, Boundary Objects, and Thicker Interfaces (18 minute read)
item.description: Current agent-planning interfaces trap people in walls of Markdown text, even though humans read roughly 240 words a minute against an agent's 4,500. Chuukese wayfinding and Susan Leigh Star's boundary-object theory frame a case for thicker, visual, interactive, and social interfaces instead of thin text exchanges. A GitHub Next prototype called Chopin explores multiplayer, real-time planning where coworkers and agents share visual, editable plans rather than solitary text approvals.

item.title: Why Canva hit the brakes on its huge AI rollout (and what other brands can learn from it) (2 minute read)
item.description: Canva revealed that overwhelming demand for Canva AI 2.0 forced it to pause the rollout, leading the company to re-engineer the platform and reduce AI processing costs by nearly 90% while making it five times faster. Rather than relying on a single AI model, Canva is investing in a diverse AI strategy focused on delivering reliable, affordable, and user-friendly experiences that can adapt as AI technology evolves.

item.title: Fitts's Law: Why the Easy Button Wins (7 minute read)
item.description: Fitts's Law, developed from 1954 cockpit-control research, holds that reaching a target gets faster as it grows larger and slower as it sits farther away. Screen edges and corners act as "magic pixels" that are effectively infinite in size on desktop, while touchscreens replace that trick with a thumb-reachable zone. The same principle for making desired actions easy to click can be inverted into dark patterns, like oversized subscribe buttons next to tiny cancel links.

item.title: Artist Turns Renaissance Paintings, Digital Fragments, and Dream Logic into Surreal Worlds That Feel More Like Memories Than Collages (1 minute read)
item.description: Since 2009, self-taught Canary Islands artist Chema Mendez has fused Renaissance paintings, photography, and AI-generated details into surreal collages that feel like resolved dream paintings, not fragments.

item.title: How Rob Farmer turns half-baked sketches into New York Times covers (3 minute read)
item.description: Australian motion designer Rob Farmer turns everyday observations into experimental design work, encouraging creatives to share imperfect ideas and embrace curiosity over perfectionism.

item.title: AI Might Kill Humanity in 10 Years, but Autodesk's CEO Sees a More Immediate Threat to Artists (4 minute read)
item.description: Autodesk CEO Andrew Anagnost calls the industry's AI-extinction talk partly "political theater" while still insisting the technology needs real guardrails.

item.title: Photoshop and Premiere Elements 2027 Make Photo and Video Easy (3 minute read)
item.description: Adobe has launched Photoshop Elements 2027 and Premiere Elements 2027 with new AI-powered features aimed at beginners, including an AI Assistant, Generative Expand, Generative Upscale, and smarter editing tools that simplify photo and video workflows. Both apps also add improved organization, contextual editing guidance, and AI-generated creative tools while maintaining their focus on ease of use over professional-grade complexity.

item.title: For the Builders: Canvas, CMS, and Quality-of-Life Improvements from Webflow Conf 2026 (8 minute read)
item.description: Webflow Conf 2026's Builder Keynote introduced canvas, CMS, and workflow updates, following 151 improvements shipped since last year based on user feedback. New launches include visual editing for AI code components, components usable directly within CMS items, and a breakpoint canvas showing all device views simultaneously. Upcoming features include popovers, default slot components, Agentic Translation, and component style props, alongside reported performance gains of up to 98% faster copying and 80% faster publishing.

item.title: iOS 27 gives Camera app on iPhone three powerful new features (3 minute read)
item.description: iOS 27 introduces major Camera app upgrades, including an AI-powered Siri mode that can understand what the camera sees, customizable camera controls, and exclusive iPhone 18 Pro features like manual aperture and shutter controls, enhanced Photographic Styles, and Apple Reference Image for verifying photo authenticity. The update also makes it easier to personalize the Camera interface by adding or removing controls based on how you shoot.

item.title: For the Designless (13 minute read)
item.description: AI hasn't changed what designers do—it has changed who can attempt design, making creative tools accessible to people who previously lacked the knowledge or budget to create effective visual communication. The key distinction is between users who genuinely benefit from AI assistance, those whose handmade work is more authentic than polished output, and businesses that use AI simply to cut corners, with the greatest value coming from helping underserved users create better, culturally relevant designs through strong visual references. The future of AI-assisted design depends less on generating attractive visuals and more on producing work that reflects local context and authentic visual traditions instead of generic, homogenized aesthetics.

item.title: Six Common Mistakes in Design Tokens Naming (4 minute read)
item.description: Weak design token names slow searches, inflate duplicates, and turn governance into guesswork, according to six recurring naming mistakes design systems teams make. Common pitfalls include naming tokens after components too early, baking current values like colors or pixel sizes directly into names, and reordering name segments inconsistently. Other traps are mixing casing and separators, using vague modifiers like "primary" without defined scope, and renaming tokens without a phased migration and alias strategy.

item.title: Designing with Children, Not for Them (6 minute read)
item.description: A free handbook from Save the Children Finland outlines how to co-design digital products with children rather than for them, through consent, play, and trust-building. Practical techniques include sitting at a child's eye level, using pictures and props instead of direct interviews, and capping group sessions at six children per two adults. Success is measured by how heard a child felt rather than what adults intended, since children lose motivation quickly and need visible, steady progress.

item.title: The Designer Who Drew Cursor's Icons (9 minute read)
item.description: Marek Minor, founder of Amsterdam studio Minor Adventures, spent a year hand-drawing Cursor's entire icon set of more than 600 icons in two sizes and styles. The set replaced Cursor's inherited VS Code Codicons, with Minor working closely with Head of Design Ryo through explorations like 156 versions of a single hamburger icon. AI helped him think through concepts and build companion tools like a migration dashboard, but he drew every icon by hand and still maintains the set today.

item.title: Product Strategy Starts with What You Will Not Build (15 minute read)
item.description: Product strategy is defined by what a team explicitly refuses to build, not merely a revenue goal paired with a feature list. Marty Cagan calls the choice of which problems to solve the strategy layer sitting above both discovery and delivery, one most companies skip entirely. Three tools do the work: Playing to Win's nested choices, Rumelt's kernel as a fluff detector, and Biddle's Netflix-born DHM, while roadmaps merely sequence the bets.

item.title: How Recent™ gave Spectrum one identity for music, wellness and place (5 minute read)
item.description: Spectrum's refreshed identity is built around three core pillars—Ritual, Pulse, and Body—which are woven into an interlaced "S" logo that symbolizes the festival's blend of music, wellness, and community. The flexible visual system uses a spectrum of purple hues, New Edge 666 typography, abstract gradients and halftones, and a practical pill-shaped information system that adapts seamlessly across signage, merchandise, and digital touchpoints. Rather than relying on clichés of Aruba or festival culture, the brand expresses the island through its content and experiences, creating a premium identity that can shift effortlessly between high-energy nightlife and calm wellness moments.

item.title: How Marie-Lou Garcia turns vacations, friendships and quiet days into serene illustrations (7 minute read)
item.description: Illustrator Marie-Lou Garcia transforms quiet personal moments into serene artwork, encouraging artists to embrace creative freedom, trust their intuition, and stay true to their craft despite industry challenges.

item.title: Canva is Quietly Publishing Nearly 1 Million Websites a Month (2 minute read)
item.description: Canva now publishes close to one million new websites every month.

item.title: The iPhone Duo's Opening Animation is a 10/10 Design Flex for Apple (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple's foldable iPhone Duo debuted an opening animation that blurs the outer screen into the inner display, creating the illusion of glass rather than a phone screen.

item.title: Meta Launched an AI That Uses Websites for You. That Could Be a Big Deal for Web Designers (3 minute read)
item.description: Meta launched Muse, a consumer AI agent built on its Muse Spark model that can navigate websites, fill forms, send emails, book travel, and make payments. The browser sub-agent reads an accessibility-tree snapshot of pages rather than the raw DOM, so semantic structure and accessibility may grow increasingly important for web designers. Reuters reported that internal testing found reliability problems, including an instance where an agent exposed personal iCloud photos, though Meta says added security work delayed the launch.

item.title: Canva launches ProSuite bringing Affinity, Cavalry, Flourish, and Leonardo together with more than 100 new features (4 minute read)
item.description: Canva has officially unified its creative acquisitions into Canva ProSuite, a connected professional toolkit that includes Affinity, Cavalry, Flourish, and Leonardo, while keeping the core Affinity and Cavalry tools free. Alongside 100 new features—including long-requested Affinity updates, automation, AI integrations, and improved interoperability—Canva is positioning itself as a serious alternative to Adobe by combining professional-grade tools with its mass-market platform, emphasizing accessible workflows over subscription-driven software.

item.title: Apple releases iOS 27 with Siri AI and these new iPhone features (2 minute read)
item.description: iOS 27 is now available, bringing Siri AI, expanded Apple Intelligence features, greater control over the Liquid Glass interface, and performance improvements across the system. Siri AI can understand personal context, interact with on-screen content, assist with writing, and work alongside new AI-powered tools in Photos and Safari, including image editing, webpage monitoring, and automatic tab grouping. The update also adds practical features like separate alarm and timer volume controls, customizable AirPods EQ, improved parental controls, faster performance, and accessibility enhancements, with Apple Intelligence available on the iPhone 15 Pro models, the iPhone 16 lineup and later, iPhone Air, and iPhone Duo.

item.title: Sustainable Accessibility: Compliance, Culture, and Capability (8 minute read)
item.description: Accessibility programs often fail not from a lack of standards or budget, but because organizations chase compliance alone while culture and capability go unbuilt. A three C's model, borrowed from the fire triangle, argues that compliance, culture, and capability must all stay lit or the whole effort burns out.

item.title: The UX Double Diamond is Dead, and in AI Only One Survives for Software (11 minute read)
item.description: The Double Diamond and Design Thinking priced building as the risky, expensive step, but AI has cut prototyping costs by orders of magnitude, collapsing that premise. As a result, front-end research and ideation shrink to a one-page brief, while generation widens and the judgment budget—evaluating and choosing among many cheap options—becomes the real bottleneck. Hardware, fashion, and regulated industries such as medical devices and payments remain exceptions where building stays costly and irreversible, so front-loading still applies there.

item.title: I'm Transitioning From UI/UX to AI UX (11 minute read)
item.description: A growing number of UX designers are shifting toward AI UX, which focuses on designing how people interact with intelligent systems rather than simply creating interfaces. Unlike traditional UX, AI UX requires designers to think about behaviors, trust, uncertainty, conversational flows, human oversight, and how AI should respond in different situations, while building on existing UX skills like user research, interaction design, and usability testing. The transition involves learning AI fundamentals, studying successful AI products, designing AI-powered experiences, and creating portfolio projects that demonstrate not just polished interfaces but thoughtful human-AI interactions and decision-making.

item.title: A Certain Subset of Designers Are Struggling with AI. Here's How to Fix It with Writing (7 minute read)
item.description: Shoot-from-the-hip designers who rely on instinct without a repeatable process tend to stall above Senior, where promotion depends on influence, not just output. Writing that instinct into a rubric, such as where the eye lands first or what decision was made, turns judgment into something an AI model can use. One Lead designer, pushed to name the user, the task, and the decision he'd made instead of "we," began building his own checks after three projects.

item.title: Too Fast to Design (2 minute read)
item.description: Design work often requires sitting with an ambiguous problem rather than jumping to a fix, like resizing a button instead of asking why people aren't clicking it. AI tends to shortcut that stage, turning a vague brief into a flow, screen, and text within seconds. That halts exploration not because the answer is wrong, but because it's reasonable enough to accept, so AI works best widening the question first.

item.title: The Digger poster design strikes graphic design gold (2 minute read)
item.description: The teaser poster for Digger stands out by embracing a minimalist, typography-led design inspired by Saul Bass, using the movie's title to form the silhouette of a figure with a spade instead of relying on the typical collage of actors and action scenes. Rather than selling the film through star power, the symbolic design captures its central idea—a man whose destructive drilling triggers an ecological disaster—creating intrigue through a single memorable visual. It highlights how modern movie marketing can still benefit from timeless graphic design principles that prioritize storytelling and symbolism over spectacle.

item.title: iPhone Duo can add fake bezel to the outside screen for better case compatibility (1 minute read)
item.description: Apple has added a new "Shift Left Edge" display option for the iPhone Duo that creates a larger left bezel to prevent cases from obscuring content on the outer screen, though it's unclear which cases will require it.

item.title: The Best Accessible Design of 2026 (1 minute read)
item.description: Fast Company named Make Good's open-source, fully 3D-printed Toddler Mobility Trainer the winner of its 2026 Innovation by Design Awards for accessible design.

item.title: Figma is Turning Designers into Plugin Makers (3 minute read)
item.description: Figma's AI agent now builds fully coded plugins from a plain-language description, handling tasks like bulk-restyling icons, generating type ramps, and flagging broken prototype flows.
